advances:
The complete parallel-side homothetic-simplex endpoint ansatz is impossible in the separated-scale all-double branch. More precisely, let \(A_2\) be a triangle, let \(A_0\) be a positive homothetic copy of \(A_2\) with area ratio \(M/m=d^2>3\), and align the three affine cutting directions with the three pairs of parallel sides. Even if \(K\) is allowed to be an arbitrary compatible convex enlargement, the three crossings, strict outer no-half inequality, all-double \(Q\)-support, and \(r_{123}>0\) are inconsistent.

The contradiction is exact. The crossing identity forces a lower bound on the sum of the six squared endpoint-cap scales, while positivity of the common middle triangle forces an upper bound on their linear sum. Together they would imply
\[
d^2-3d+3<0,
\]
although
\[
d^2-3d+3=\left(d-\frac32\right)^2+\frac34>0.
\]
Thus neither changing the offsets nor enlarging \(K\) can rescue this whole ansatz. Any surviving separated-scale construction must break at least one of the two aligned-simplex features: triangular homothety of the endpoints or parallelism of the three cutting directions with the corresponding sides.

proof:
The cap \(P_i^+\) is a triangle similar to \(A_0\), with linear scale \(p_i\), while \(C_i\) is a triangle similar to \(A_2\), with linear scale \(s_i\). Therefore
\[
|P_i^+|=\frac{p_i^2}{2},
\qquad
x_i=|C_i|=\frac{s_i^2}{2}.
\tag{7}
\]
The complementary \(P\)-marginal is
\[
u_i=M-|P_i^+|
=\frac{d^2-p_i^2}{2}.
\tag{8}
\]
Because the all-double support has only \(Q_{123}\) and the three caps \(C_i\),
\[
q=m-x_1-x_2-x_3
=\frac{1-s_1^2-s_2^2-s_3^2}{2}.
\tag{9}
\]
Put
\[
U=u_1+u_2+u_3,
\qquad
E_R=r_{12}+r_{13}+r_{23}+2r_{123}.
\]
Equations (8)-(9) give
\[
U+q
=
\frac{
3d^2+1-\sum_i p_i^2-\sum_i s_i^2
}{2}.
\tag{10}
\]

We first extract the linear cap-scale constraint. From (5),
\[
\tau_i=d+a_i-p_i,
\qquad
\lambda_i=1-s_i.
\]
Using \(\sum_i a_i=1-d\), one obtains
\[
\sum_i\tau_i=1+2d-P,
\qquad
\sum_i\lambda_i=3-S.
\]
Equation (4) therefore gives
\[
\sum_i\rho_i
=2+d-\frac{P+S}{2}.
\tag{11}
\]
But (1) gives \(\sum_i\rho_i=1+1/\alpha>1\). Hence
\[
P+S<2d+2.
\tag{12}
\]
Geometrically, (12) is exactly the positive-scale condition for the common middle triangle \(\{z_i\leq\rho_i\}\); it is also necessary for \(r_{123}>0\).

We next extract the squared cap-scale constraint from the crossings. Under all-double support,
\[
\sum_i v_i=2m+q,
\]
and exact middle-cell counting gives
\[
\sum_i c_i=k+E_R.
\]
Summing \(u_i+v_i+c_i=h\), where \(3h=2(M+m+k)/3\), gives the exact identity
\[
2M=4m+k+3(U+q+E_R).
\tag{13}
\]
Write
\[
e^2=2k.
\]
Substituting \(M=d^2/2\), \(m=1/2\), and (10) into (13), and using
\[
E_R\geq2r_{123}>0,
\]
gives
\[
3\left(\sum_i p_i^2+\sum_i s_i^2\right)
>
7d^2+7+e^2.
\tag{14}
\]
The strict no-half inequality (6) is
\[
\frac{d^2}{2}<\frac12+\frac{e^2}{2},
\]
so
\[
e^2>d^2-1.
\tag{15}
\]
Combining (14) and (15) yields the strict lower bound
\[
3\left(\sum_i p_i^2+\sum_i s_i^2\right)
>8d^2+6.
\tag{16}
\]

On the other hand, (5) gives
\[
\sum_i p_i^2<dP,
\qquad
\sum_i s_i^2<S.
\]
Since \(d>1\), equation (12) implies
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_i p_i^2+\sum_i s_i^2
&<dP+S\\
&=d(P+S)-(d-1)S\\
&<2d^2+2d.
\end{aligned}
\tag{17}
\]
Equations (16)-(17) would force
\[
8d^2+6<6d^2+6d,
\]
or
\[
d^2-3d+3<0.
\tag{18}
\]
But
\[
d^2-3d+3
=\left(d-\frac32\right)^2+\frac34>0
\]
for every real \(d\). This contradiction proves the statement.

No property of the shape of \(K\) was used beyond its exact middle cells, the crossings, and (6). Thus replacing the midpoint triangle by any controlled convex enlargement cannot evade the contradiction. The proof is confined to the aligned homothetic-simplex endpoint ansatz and makes no claim for nonparallel endpoint cuts or nontriangular endpoint bodies.
statement:
Work in the affine plane
\[
\Pi=\{(z_1,z_2,z_3)\in\mathbb R^3:z_1+z_2+z_3=1\}
\]
with the area normalization for which
\[
\Delta=\{z\in\Pi:z_i\geq0\ (i=1,2,3)\}
\]
has area \(1/2\). Let
\[
A_2=\Delta,
\qquad
A_0=a+d\Delta
=\{a+dy:y\in\Delta\},
\]
where \(d>1\), \(\sum_i a_i=1-d\), and hence
\[
m=\frac12,\qquad M=\frac{d^2}{2}.
\]
This includes \(A_0=z_\ast+d(A_2-z_\ast)\) whenever \(d\ne1\), with
\[
z_\ast=\frac{a}{1-d}.
\]

Assume the aligned affine functions have the form
\[
f_i(z)=\alpha(z_i-\rho_i),
\qquad
\alpha>0,
\qquad
\sum_i\rho_i=1+\frac1\alpha,
\tag{1}
\]
so \(f_1+f_2+f_3=-1\) and their linear parts are pairwise nonparallel. Let \(L_1+L_2+L_3<-1\), and define the two endpoint cut levels
\[
\tau_i=\rho_i+\frac{L_i}{\alpha},
\qquad
\lambda_i=\rho_i-\frac{L_i}{\alpha}.
\tag{2}
\]
Thus
\[
P_i^+=A_0\cap\{z_i>\tau_i\},
\qquad
C_i=Q_{N\setminus\{i\}}
=A_2\cap\{z_i>\lambda_i\},
\tag{3}
\]
up to the exact null cutting-line convention, and
\[
\rho_i=\frac{\tau_i+\lambda_i}{2}.
\tag{4}
\]

Suppose all one-cut endpoint caps in (3) are proper and positive. Put
\[
p_i=d+a_i-\tau_i\in(0,d),
\qquad
s_i=1-\lambda_i\in(0,1),
\tag{5}
\]
and abbreviate
\[
P=p_1+p_2+p_3,\qquad S=s_1+s_2+s_3.
\]
Assume the positive \(Q\)-support is exactly
\[
\{123,12,13,23\},
\]
with \(q=q_{123}>0\). Let \(K\subset\Pi\) be any two-dimensional compact convex body satisfying
\[
\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\subseteq K,
\]
and use the exact middle cells of accepted fact `0e51a47a9add571f`. Assume
\[
r_1r_2r_3r_{123}>0,
\]
the three crossings and \(W=0\), the canonical tails, and the strict outer no-half inequality
\[
M<m+k.
\tag{6}
\]
Then no such configuration exists. In particular, none exists in the required separated-scale range \(d>\sqrt3\).
